Super prototype → usable development MVP

Audited 2026-09-07 against site/app-prototype.html, current cockpit/ui, cockpit/src/bots.rs, Ampd.Projection.operator/0, and Ampd.CommandSpec. The prototype is a simulated design reference. Its numbers and bot grants are not live app records. Existing local modifications were retained.

Acceptance target

Use Super to develop Super: select its repository and workspace, create a goal, choose a persistent planning or implementation bot, delegate bounded development work, observe progress and blockers, review a real diff and validation results, accept or reject the change, and recover that same work after restart.

The app currently supports conversation and reviewed setup proposals. This pass improves that usable surface; the full development cycle still needs the runtime and editor work below. A worker assignment does not start coding.

This pass

Implemented the first five rows' conversational/UI scope and added directory summary statistics. Profiles and groups are local presentation records. Bot pages explicitly identify the runtime delegation gap. This pass does not expose a fake Delegate button, fabricate agent activity, or turn profiles into runtime actors.

No runtime stores, grants, command allowlists, or authority rules were modified. Graphonomous tools were not available in this session; the existing task notes, repository instructions and current source supplied continuity.

Remaining MVP sequence

  1. Define and implement actor-bound bots and scoped observation projections.

  2. Implement and verify durable capability delegation and revocation semantics.

  3. Connect bounded execution to repository worktrees and real diff review.

  4. Finish record-level flags, evidence paging, cancellation and recovery UX.

  5. Perform the full Super-on-Super acceptance workflow with a real provider.

Validation results for the present UI pass are recorded in the delivery report.

Continued pass: runtime bot identities

Implemented explicit workspace registration, versioned profile editing and guarded removal through the ordered runtime. The directory now has actor-bound bot records in the existing loci store, with own-identity visibility on the existing agent projection. Native bot pages reflect confirming frames and retain local histories. Store restart and complete process restart preserve identity without adding grants.

The registry portion of the first remaining stage is complete. Actor-authenticated execution and the prototype's full scoped-observation/citation contract remain open. The next stage is real parent/child delegation, followed by bounded coding execution and diff review. Keep Bots for individuals; reserve Swarms for that coordinated team workflow. See the runtime contract.

Continued pass: Editor, Terminal, and Browser

Added the two requested Nav destinations beneath Editor and connected the manual local development loop: native repository selection, folder browsing, text editing and saving with conflict checks, real command execution with bounded output and process-group stopping, and an isolated local-browser preview. Linux preview layout uses an overlay so the browser remains inside its page without shrinking the cockpit.

This completes the manual inspect/edit/run/preview tools. It does not complete the P0 worktree/diff-review stage or give bots execution authority. The remaining MVP sequence above still applies to the autonomous runtime workflow. The next connection must tie registered bot actors and delegated work to worktrees, validation evidence, and reviewed changes. See the tool contract.

Verified: 18 native development-flow checks, 90 existing native app checks, 24 Rust tests (one unrelated desktop attachment test ignored), 18 JavaScript tests, and 35 WebView ACL checks. Release build and whitespace checks passed.

Tabbed workbench follow-up

The development pages now use flat, full-height panels with file, interactive PTY and native browser tabs. CodeMirror provides real syntax highlighting and editor controls. Local shells survive navigation, and runtime workers with PRESENT terminals can be selected for the existing read-only watch transport. Explicit bot attachments link back to a file, shell, watched worker or browser tab. Window edges initiate native resize; Linux browser layout releases the main view minimum so active previews can shrink with the window.

Remaining P0 execution work: register agent-owned sessions with stable IDs and bot/lane/workspace ownership; connect admitted coding operations and cancellation; restore or clearly terminate ownership on restart; deliver execution and review results. Swarm delegation should share this registry, rather than discovering arbitrary processes or inventing browser/terminal ownership. See LOCAL_DEVELOPMENT.md.

Second prototype comparison: saved-change review and record guidance

Added read-only Git changes in Editor, record section tabs and scoped setup flags and worker-state bars. Reduced repeated session-control rebuilding and shell-output copying. The rich landing page still has measured WebKit painting lag; pausing its animation alone does not fix scrolling. The next P0 work is shared agent session ownership, delegation, bounded coding, revision-bound validation/acceptance and restart recovery. See the second-pass audit for implementation details, limits, priorities and current test results.

Workbench continuity follow-up

Implemented device-local file-tab and draft recovery, explicit browser-address restoration, ended-shell notices, recovery-copy management and patch snapshots attached to bot conversations. Draft recovery preserves native conflict detection and does not reopen repository access or execute commands automatically. See the recovery contract. This closes part of manual workbench continuity; agent-owned execution, Swarm delegation and revision-bound validation/acceptance remain open.

Bot work continuation — 2026-09-07

Conversation/Work tabs now show bot-owned lanes and workers, terminal availability, and real setup/detail actions. The complete bot → lane → worker path exposed and fixed a shared text-field prefill bug. Repository registration now follows the working native development chooser pattern. See BOT_WORK_PAGES_2026_09_07.md for scope and verification. Durable agent sessions, delegation, coding admission, cancellation and recovery remain open.

Shared sessions and reviewed coding — 2026-09-07

Native human-operated shells and browser tabs can now be linked to bot Work pages, reopened without recreating them, and preserved across main-page reload. Typed single-file provider proposals can be compared in Editor, staged as unsaved drafts and explicitly saved with disk-conflict protection. The isolated native provider-to-preview flow is verified; a real signed-in-provider dogfooding request is waiting on automatic approval review of its exact source payload/destination. See SHARED_SESSIONS_AND_CODE_REVIEW_2026_09_07.md. Swarm delegation and actor-authenticated execution remain separate open runtime work.
